title: Self-Adaptive Modality Routing for Multimodal Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a self-adaptive controller that dynamically selects when an agent workflow should invoke visual reasoning, textual reasoning, or both reduce unnecessary multimodal calls while improving end-task accuracy under changing input difficulty?
hypothesis: A MAPE-K-style controller that monitors uncertainty and task context, then routes subtasks to text-only, vision-language, or hybrid reasoning modes, will outperform static multimodal pipelines by improving cost-accuracy trade-offs and reducing failures caused by overconfident single-model selection.
motivation: The knowledge base shows an explicit open problem around extending self-adaptive uncertainty handling to additional domains and heterogeneous optimization goals. At the same time, several nearby agent-orchestration ideas have already been rejected, especially those focused on uncertainty averaging, escalation, and verifier-guided decomposition. This suggests a gap: instead of proposing yet another generic uncertainty-aware orchestrator, a more novel direction is to transfer self-adaptive model-selection ideas into multimodal agent workflows, where the key decision is not just which agent to call, but whether visual reasoning is necessary at all. This targets a practical bottleneck in multimodal systems—high cost, latency, and brittle routing—while remaining distinct from the rejected ideas by centering on adaptive modality selection rather than general orchestration or Bayesian averaging alone.
